Investigations/ALX-01 · Flagship

Forensic investigation of Amazon Alexa-enabled IoT devices

Evaluating cloud-based evidence acquisition and forensic artefact interpretation across Amazon Echo Dot and Echo Show.

01

Project introduction

Amazon Echo devices keep little on the device itself and hold much of their evidence in the cloud. This research asked what an investigator can recover through an official route, a GDPR Subject Access Request, and how reliable and complete that evidence is.

Two devices were studied: an Echo Show whose telemetry covered 160 days, and an Echo Dot used in a controlled test over 23 days. The two data sets turned out to hold different kinds of evidence.

Academic researchThe scenario is a simulated household burglary between 01:00 and 03:00. This is a research investigation, not a real-world criminal case.

03

Research question

How can cloud-hosted digital evidence obtained through official data access mechanisms be acquired, examined and interpreted during an IoT forensic investigation?

Objectives

  • Literature and frameworks. Examine IoT forensic research and the difficulties it reports.
  • Artefact analysis. Identify and examine artefacts in data obtained through the SAR process.
  • Comparative evaluation. Compare findings with current models and literature to judge how well existing methods cope.
04

Background and context

Echo hardware uses encryption and proprietary firmware, which makes conventional imaging impractical. Evidence is spread across the device, the companion app and Amazon's cloud, and no standard procedure exists for IoT forensics. The forensic value of SAR data had not been thoroughly evaluated.

What is a Subject Access Request?

Under Article 15 of the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, an account holder can ask a company for a copy of the personal data it holds. Amazon accepted the request through its privacy portal and returned a ZIP archive about one week later. The route is read-only: it cannot alter Amazon's data.

Why a simulated burglary?

The scenario gave the data a purpose. It framed the Echo Dot as a possible exhibit and let the analysis ask what each artefact could say about the 01:00 to 03:00 window, without implying that any real offence took place.

05

Evidence sources

  • Echo Show telemetry. 1,296 log entries across 12 namespaces, 2025-08-10 to 2026-01-16. Network, system and device-state data only.
  • Echo Dot behavioural data. Voice utterances, call history, music activity, sensor readings, messaging and account settings, 2026-02-11 onward.
  • The archive. 32 files in CSV, XLSX, HTML and JSON, delivered as a single ZIP.
06

Tools and technologies

Amazon GDPR SARPythonGoogle ColaboratoryMagnet AXIOM Examine v9.10Seaborn / Matplotlib

No forensic tool was found that parses Amazon SAR archives in a standardised way. Google Colaboratory was the only viable analysis platform identified, and AXIOM served as a cross-check.

07

Acquisition methodology

  1. ScenarioDevelop the simulated burglary and the two-device design.
  2. RequestSubmit the SAR through Amazon's privacy portal using the account holder's own login.
  3. ReceiveArchive delivered about a week after the request. Original ZIP kept unaltered.
  4. Analyse copiesAll processing done on working copies, with an audit trail of dates.

ACPO principles. The SAR route is read-only, so no data was altered at source. A record of request and receipt dates was kept.

LimitationHash verification was not used, because the SAR process offers no independent source to verify against.

09

Findings

Confirmedverified directly in the investigation outputRecoveredartefact recovered from the evidencePotentialpresent but not shown to be user-initiatedInterpretationanalytical readingHypothesisworking idea, untestedLimitationconstraint on what can be claimed
Echo Show

Echo Show

Evidence relating primarily to technical device activity.

  • Wi-Fi signal and network configuration
  • Device uptime and firmware integrity
  • One precisely timed connectivity anomaly
Echo Dot

Echo Dot

Evidence relating primarily to human behaviour.

  • Spoken commands with timestamps
  • Drop-In calls, music history, sensor readings
  • Partial messaging content

Echo Show: technical device activity

  • ConfirmedNetwork identity. The same router identity and network were reported across all 108 Wi-Fi entries over 160 days, on WPA2-PSK. Identifiers are withheld on this page.
  • ConfirmedFirmware. Update count was 0 across 108 entries and one OS version was recorded throughout.
  • ConfirmedUptime. The boot counter increased steadily across the 160 days, so no reboot or power cycle was recorded.
  • ConfirmedConnectivity anomaly. A 16-second outage on 2025-08-10 between 21:54:04Z and 21:54:20Z. A latency peak of 2,613 ms on the same date came from a second namespace.
  • RecoveredPrivate network only. 108 captive-portal entries were blank, consistent with no public Wi-Fi use.
  • LimitationNo user records. The Echo Show export held no voice, call or message artefacts. A separate SAR export would be needed.

Echo Dot: human behaviour

  • RecoveredVoice utterances. The dissertation reports 110 recoverable utterances, each with a millisecond timestamp. Music and playback was the largest category.
  • RecoveredDrop-In. Two incoming events: 2026-02-16 (63 s) and 2026-02-19 (33 s), both with audio and video streams, classed PRIVATE.
  • RecoveredMusic history. 61 tracks across Amazon Music and Apple Music, with track-level detail.
  • RecoveredTemperature sensor. 1,025 readings, mean 21.3 °C, range 19.1 to 24.2 °C. This sensor is specific to the 5th generation Echo Dot.
  • RecoveredMessaging. Two threads with partial content from test messages on 2026-03-06.
  • LimitationSpeaker attribution gap. No active voice profile was shown in two snapshots, so speech cannot be tied to a speaker.

What an unexplained status can and cannot show

InterpretationThe Echo Dot logged 127 connectivity entries: 60 OK and 67 UNREACHABLE (52.8%). In the controlled test, every power cycle between sessions produced an UNREACHABLE entry. Taken alone, such entries cannot prove interference.

Cross-device comparison

Artefact categoryEcho ShowEcho DotWhy it matters
Device uptime and reboot historyPresentAbsentSupports that the device was not powered off or reset.
Firmware and update historyPresentAbsentIntegrity can be assessed for the Echo Show only.
Network identityPresentAbsentSupports location checks from the Echo Show only.
Latency and anomaly logsPresentAbsentOnly the Echo Show can evidence a network disturbance.
Captive portal / network typePresentAbsentIndicates a private network throughout.
Voice utterances with timestampsAbsentPresentOnly the Echo Dot can show whether anyone spoke to it.
Music and media activityAbsentPresentCan place a person using the device at a given time.
Call and Drop-In historyAbsentPresentCan show real-time communication.
Messaging artefactsAbsentPresentPartial content was recovered.

12

Limitations and challenges

  • LimitationLimited data scope. One account and two devices limit how far results generalise.
  • LimitationNo hash verification. The SAR process offers no independent source to verify against, which limits formal chain of custody.
  • LimitationNo standard tooling. No forensic tool parses Amazon SAR data. AXIOM treated the archive as generic documents and did not reconstruct cross-file timelines or surface the connectivity warnings.
  • LimitationPlatform choice. Google Colaboratory was the viable analytical platform, but it sends data to Google's servers, which raises chain-of-custody questions in formal settings.
  • LimitationNo coordinates. The export held no latitude or longitude.
  • LimitationDeleted data and third parties. Data deleted before the request cannot be recovered, and the archive may hold other people's personal data.
13

Technical skills demonstrated

14

Final investigative takeaway

Cross-device analysis gives a more complete forensic picture than examining either device on its own.

The Echo Dot shows what a person did. The Echo Show shows what the device and network did. The 16-second anomaly is a precisely timed lead, but this research does not claim it proves the simulated burglary. It is an academic investigation, not a criminal prosecution.
